dogecoin.text: @Ivan_D_Crypto Trust Wallet is quite confusing, but here you can see real #Dogecoin (on top) and Binance-Doge (as a BEP2 token) below it. To figure out which one is the real one you must tap on the asset and see which one says "COIN" (the real Doge) and which one says "BEP2" or "BEP20". Check: https://t.co/2Gf6ruwdcx

If you hold #Dogecoin as Binance-Doge, you are throwing away the permissionless and decentralized nature of the  Doge network, its sovereignty, for a centralized token on a network controlled by the largest exchange in the world. 

This kills everything Doge is meant to be.

You are not powerless:

- Do not hold on exchanges, hold in your own private wallet
- Avoid lending programs like Gemini/FTX/Voyager Earn: they lend your crypto to speculators like Barry Silbert
- Do not hold Doge as a centralized IOU like BSC-Doge

Take back control, #Dogecoin!

Binance "Bridge" is just one entity emitting tokens and putting some collateral in some wallets (hopefully). #dogecoin

About the so-called Binance "Bridge" - I answered this several times, but it might be lost in sub-tweets. 

The "Bridge" is literally "just" Binance itself. You get one of these tokenized assets, like Binance-Doge, by withdrawing through the BSC or BNB network. 

#Dogecoin

Let me correct this glaring thing: more than BSC-Doge, we should obviously call it more generically "Binance-pegged Doge", as it exists in both the Binance Smart Chain (as BEP20) and BNB Beacon chain (as BEP2). #Dogecoin

Some Binance-tokenized cryptos have Proof of Assets covering 90% of the wrapped token circulating supply. but most have way less than that. Check ETH, LTC, ADA, FIL (!?), for example.

I wonder what is the percentage for Dogecoin, since it is not even shown in that page?

For the 1000th time: we have no idea when and how this is backed by real #Dogecoin, as Binance is being completely opaque about this, as they are NOT providing a "Proof of Assets" entry for Doge as they do for all other major (and not so major) cryptos:

https://t.co/7M9bSW6JfO

Since 93% of the supply of the BEP2 token is held in a single (Binance's) wallet (against 25% of the BEP20 token on BSC), I assume most of the BEP2 BSC-Doge is just sitting there, you know, just in case. #Dogecoin

Interesting bit: this other one is the BEP2 tokenized version, which has again a theoretical supply of 1.6B Doge (!!!) but "only" 35k holders. #Dogecoin

https://t.co/ltUEqHawuN

When sending BSC-Doge back to Binance to convert it back into real #Dogecoin, it is important that you pick the right chain/standard (BEP2 or BEP20) depending on the kind of wrapped Doge you have withdrawn from @Binance in the past.

The deposit addresses are different: https://t.co/o5bSxKCmjr
